episodes.184150: Severe storms developed along a slowly moving frontal boundary on the afternoon of September 25, producing wind damage across the region. The area around Edna was especially hard hit with widespread wind damage and a brief tornado.
episodes.184151: As storms along a frontal boundary advanced offshore, several observation sites along the coast reported strong wind gusts.
episodes.184202: Higher moisture across southern New Mexico along with lift from a subtle disturbance resulted in the development of scattered showers and storms across south central and southeast New Mexico. Some storms produced nickel sized hail in southern Socorro County and at Corona in Lincoln County.
episodes.184620: Southerly steering flow lifted a frontal zone from central FL northward with an increase in deeper moisture with PWAT nearing 2 inches. These ingredients combined with a passing short-wave trough produced isolated storms with locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.184621: A weak surface front was near the FL-GA state-line with moist, unstable conditions south of the boundary across NE FL. Diurnally enhanced storms further intensified into the afternoon and early evening as a short-wave trough moved across the area from the west. Storm motion was slow, so locally heavy rainfall was a concern near storm mergers.
episodes.184622: A weak surface front was near the FL-GA state-line with moist, unstable conditions south of the boundary across NE FL. Diurnally enhanced storms further intensified into the afternoon and early evening as a short-wave trough moved across the area from the west. Storm motion was slow, so locally heavy rainfall was a concern near storm mergers.
episodes.184623: A weak surface front was near the FL-GA state-line with moist, unstable conditions south of the boundary across NE FL. Diurnally enhanced storms further intensified into the afternoon and early evening as a short-wave trough moved across the area from the west. Storm motion was slow, so locally heavy rainfall was a concern near storm mergers. North of the boundary enhanced onshore flow near the GA Coast produced locally heavy rainfall in a convergent band during the morning.
episodes.184763: A nearly stationary frontal boundary draped across central Illinois served as the focusing mechanism for clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms during the evening of September 26th.  The storms grew more numerous and vigorous as the nocturnal low-level jet nosed into the region.  As a result, a few of the cells were able to produce damaging wind gusts of around 60 mph and hail as large as quarters.
episodes.184834: Heavy rain caused localized flooding in parts of Chicago during the morning of September 26th.
episodes.184922: Many strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening across southeast New Mexico and along the higher elevations with a passing shortwave trough.
episodes.185055: Surface low pressure passed through the area, bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms. Some thunderstorms became strong to severe, producing small hail and gusty winds. Several reports of funnel clouds were received, with one weak tornado reported.
episodes.185674: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a stalled cold front/outflow boundary positioned across portions of the Permian Basin and Lower Trans Pecos.
episodes.185749: A thunderstorm produced severe wind gusts near the Sanford Airport in Seminole County.
episodes.185750: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and Treasure Coasts.
episodes.185904: Scattered thunderstorms formed over the Victoria Crossroads during the early evening hours. The storms moved through the coastal waters of the northern Coastal Bend in the evening, producing wind gusts between 35 and 45 knots.
episodes.186079: A surge of moisture moved into the El Paso area from the east as a weak upper disturbance moved along the International Border.  Enough instability and shear lead to severe thunderstorms and flash flooding in El Paso.
episodes.186134: As a deep upper trough moved further west into the western Gulf Mexico, high pressure was in the process of rebuilding north of the Florida Keys.  Speed convergency resulting from the increased east-southeast flow aided in the development of widespread showers and thunderstorms, including scattered gale-force convective wind gusts.
episodes.186151: A pair of high wind gusts recorded from isolated severe storms in Louisiana.
episodes.187149: A stalled surface boundary extending from near Kansas City through central Illinois provided a focus for organized convection during the afternoon. Thunderstorms were mainly hail producers, with up to 1.75 inch diameter hailstones reported in the St. Louis metropolitan area.

events.narrative: Two power poles were reported blown down in rural Terrell County. Time is estimated from radar. Wind speeds are estimated to be approximately 90 mph. Property damage cost is an estimation.
A wind gust of 45 mph was observed at the Levee WxFlow site as a strong storm moved through the area.
A wind gust of 60 mph was observed at the Galveston North Jetty site as a strong thunderstorm moved offshore.
A wind gust of 50 mph was observed at the Oneil Rd mesonet site along the Bolivar Peninsula as a strong thunderstorm moved through the area.
A wind gust of 52 mph was observed at the Houston Kiteboard Club mesonet site as a strong thunderstorm moved through the area.
A mesonet station in Bunnell measured 2.89 inches in about 1 hour.
A mesonet station in Crescent City measured 2.81 inches in about 1 hour.
A wind gust of 42 mph was observed at the East Matagorda TCOON mesonet site.

Widespread straight line wind damage was reported across parts of Jackson County as a strong thunderstorm moved through the area. This included extensive tree damage as well as damage to power lines and some buildings.
Eye witness observed small funnel passing over eastern end of Cottonwood Apartments, damaging a building there, then proceeding to strike a metal storage unit. Swirling tin, debris was observed.
A 50-knot wind gust was measured at the FM 456 mesonet site as a strong thunderstorm moved through the Van Vleck area.

NOS site at Rockport measured a gust to 34 knots.
Rockport-Aransas County Airport ASOS measured a gust to 35 knots.

A public weather station measured 5.3 inches of storm total rainfall just west of Mt. Pleasant Road. Numerous public stations between McCormick Road to Atlantic Blvd and between Girvin Road and Kernan Blvd measured 4-5 inches of rainfall as well. Most of this rainfall occurred in the early evening.

A public weather station just west of Atlantic Beach Elementary School measured storm total rainfall of 4.65 inches by 8 pm. Other public weather stations in the area measured 3-4.5 inches of daily rainfall.

A public weather station along Lakeshore Drive, north of the St. Augustine airport, measured 6.67 inches of storm total daily rainfall. Another location just north along Sophia Terrace measured 6.58 inches of daily rainfall.

A public weather station along Pecan Park Road just west of Interstate 95 measured a daily storm total rainfall of 4.49 inches. Other stations in the area measured 2-4 inches of daily storm total rainfall.
As of 12:40 pm, the St. Simons Island ASOS had measured 4.50 inches of daily rainfall. This broke the existing daily rainfall record of 4.40 inches set in 1953.
The daily measured rainfall at the Camden County EOC surpassed 5 inches around 6:13 pm.

A public weather station just south of the St. Simons Island airport near Mallery Street measured a daily storm total rainfall of 6.7 inches. Other public weather stations in the area around the airport measured between 5-7 inches of daily rainfall.

events.narrative: A vertical, mature and elephant-trunk-like waterspout was observed south of Big Pine Key.  The condensation cloud extended from the cloud base to the horizon.  The observer estimated the location was south of Coupon Bight.   The waterspout moved toward the northeast around 15 knots.
Emergency Management confirmed a brief EF-U tornado several miles west of Vinton. Spotters reported a ground circulation lofting corn leaves, beneath the funnel. No damage was noted.

A witness reported a land spout that last for about 4 minutes and tracked WSW to ENE across a construction site just south of Sandridge Road near Feed Mill Road.  The vortex crossed over a construction site where it lifted garbage debris and dust. Structure damage did not occur.

The public reported a landspout touchdown just west of the Shands Bridge near Green Cove Springs. The time of the event was based on radar. The width of the tornado was approximated. There was not noted damage.
A discrete supercell produced pea to quarter sized hail as it weakened over Jefferson County.
Florida Power and Light (FPL) reported that a tree or branch damaged electrical equipment near Sherry Lane. The time of damage was based on radar.

Significant flooding, including inundation into at least 2 homes at the time of the report, occurred along and east of U.S. Highway 1 near Palencia. Flood water covered neighborhood roads north of the St. Augustine Airport to Palencia. The 2 homes that were flooded at the time of the report were along Palmetto Drive. Radar and ground truth rainfall measurements were 6-8 inches across these areas over 2 hours. There was also street flooding reported in historic downtown St Augustine along Cordova St a known flood-prone area.
A trained spotter reported storm total rainfall of 2.07 inches just southwest of Ferguson, with 1.78 of that total falling between midnight and 0530CDT.
A wind gust of 64 mph was recorded at the Lake Charles Regional Airport.

At 6 pm, the public shared images of significant street flooding at the intersection of Hendricks Avenue and Atlantic Blvd in San Marco. Local broadcast media relayed reports of flooding across streets in San Marco. Pictures showed stalled vehicles in water 6-12 inches deep.
The eastbound lanes of the Arlington Expressway near the Matthews Bridge were flooded.

A discrete thunderstorm produced mainly half inch to nickel sized hailstones in southern St. Louis County according to emergency managers, trained spotters, and the public. There was one public report of one inch hail supported by a photo of the hailstone.

A 16-year-old female died of her injuries after being struck by lightning while hunting with her father near Bostwick. Both were sheltering under a tree when storms approached. Lightning struck the tree, knocking both unconscious. The teen was hospitalized, but she passed away 2 days later.
KOPL in Opelousas recorded a wind gust of 61 mph.
Emergency management replayed a report of ping pong ball size hail in Crossroads. Time is estimated from radar.
